* [007 — HellaJS declares its own global JSX namespace in the dom barrel (packages/dom/lib/index.ts) — Element = HellaNode & RenderFn, not React](entries/007.md) — Verified 2026-07-28. Despite tsconfig `jsx: react-jsx` (a red herring that points at React), @hellajs/dom declares the global JSX namespace itself in its barrel — packages/dom/lib/index.ts:23-32, inside `declare global`: `Element = HellaNode & RenderFn` (render-fns ARE HellaNodes type-wise, via intersection), `IntrinsicElements extends HTMLAttributeMap`, `ElementAttributesProperty.props`, `ElementChildrenAttribute.children`. So JSX.Element = HellaNode & RenderFn, assignable to ComponentReturn (HellaNode | (() => HellaNode)) — load-bearing for component() typing and any render-fn type reasoning. * [016 — bun:test's expect(promise).rejects.toThrow() must be awaited — an unawaited matcher silently false-passes and leaves the rejection path uncovered](entries/016.md) — Verified 2026-07-12. In bun:test, expect(asyncThatRejects()).rejects.toThrow('msg') returns a Promise; without `await`, the test function returns before the assertion settles — the test passes whether or not the rejection actually fires, AND the rejection code path stays uncovered (coverage drops). Always write `await expect(...).rejects.toThrow(...)` (and `await` any `.resolves` matcher). · `triggers: rejects-matcher, unresolved-promise-assertion, bun-test-async, coverage-drop-rejection, false-pass` · `tags: testing, bun-test, async, coverage` · `type: decision`
* [018 — Router SSR is library territory — router({ url }) + synchronous init make the router server-runnable; no new primitive, no per-request rewrite for the sync path](entries/018.md) — Verified 2026-07-14. Router SSR is a library feature, NOT meta-framework territory (supersedes 017). RouterConfig.url resolves the initial route against a supplied URL instead of window.location, and router() init is now synchronous (direct updateRoute(), not queueMicrotask) — so router({ routes, url: pathname+search }); ssr(App()) runs on the server with no window, and the client omits url (reads window.location) then hydrate(App()). The view-signal handler pattern () => currentView(X) is the isomorphic style. Composes with existing ssr/ssrAsync/ssrStream + hydrate; no new primitive, no per-request rewrite for the sync path. · `triggers: router-ssr, isomorphic-routing, router-url-option, synchronous-init` · `tags: arch, ssr, router, isomorphic` · `type: decision`
* [019 — HappyDOM window.location.pathname is 'blank' (about:blank) and history.replaceState({}, '', '/') does NOT change it — router() init resolves 'blank', firing notFound for unmatched routes](entries/019.md) — Verified 2026-07-14. In the test env (utils/happydom.js GlobalRegistrator), window.location.pathname is the literal string 'blank' (about:blank), NOT '/'. setupRouterEnv's window.history.replaceState({}, '', '/') is a no-op for pathname. So router() — now with synchronous init — resolves the initial path 'blank', matches no route, and fires notFound during router(). Tests asserting handler/notFound call-counts immediately after router() must isolate the init firing (mockClear() after router()) or assert state (route().path/handler), since init is no longer deferred past the assertion. A test-env quirk, not production behavior. · `triggers: happydom-location, router-test-init, blank-pathname, notfound-call-count` · `tags: testing, router, happydom, env` · `type: decision`
* [020 — consumeRegion captured `next` AFTER removeChild → null (fixed: capture before removal)](entries/020.md) — Verified+fixed 2026-07-17. `consumeRegion` (`packages/dom/lib/internal/hydrate.ts`) returned `next: close.nextSibling` AFTER `parent.removeChild(close)` — a detached node's `nextSibling` is `null` per spec, and HappyDOM is spec-compliant (verified empirically: `b.nextSibling` → null after `removeChild(b)`). So every region-adoption caller (reactive child, fragment, isDynamic ForEach/Transition/Portal/Lazy/Suspense, raw) got `next=null` when a region was followed by a sibling, causing the sibling to hydrate-mismatch → fresh-mount-append → a DUPLICATE node + lost binding. Latent because no prior test paired a region with a following element sibling. Fix: capture `const next = close.nextSibling` before the `removeChild` calls. Full hydrate-adoption suite re-verified green after. · `triggers: consumeRegion, hydrate-region-adoption, nextSibling-after-remove, region-sibling-misalign` · `tags: arch, dom, hydration` · `type: correction`
* [021 — ssr.stream is pull-driven — the producer advances one chunk per pull; a test acting at a gating chunk (the <!--hs sentinel, a Lazy region-open) must await delay(0) so the NEXT pull runs the gated work first](entries/021.md) — ssrStream's ReadableStream enqueues ONLY inside pull() — each pull advances the shared generator one chunk, and the pull that follows a read fires only after that read resolves; a test that cancels/releases/asserts right after reading a gating chunk races that next pull — drain to the chunk, then `await delay(0)` so the pull runs the gated producer step (`pending.push`, `loader()`), else the cancel/swap-return/loader paths stay unexercised (or the test's resolver is still undefined). · `triggers: ssrstream-cancel-test, suspense-staged-swap, pull-driven-timing, streaming-test-tick, coverage-uncovered-cancel` · `tags: testing, ssr, streaming, bun-test, coverage` · `type: decision`

* [023 — HellaJS monorepo convention — all cross-package HellaJS deps are peerDependencies with carets; devDependencies are null everywhere; css is the sole package with a runtime dep (csstype — see Evidence)](entries/023.md) — Every packages/* package.json declares cross-pkg HellaJS deps ONLY as peerDependencies with caret ranges (ssr->dom ^1.4.2; dom/router/css/store/resource->core ^1.0.6); devDependencies are null across the board; css is the sole package with a runtime dep — csstype (^3.1.3), legitimate because CSS.Properties flows into the public CSSObject type shipped in dist/types.d.ts (consumers need it resolvable to type-check css({...}); import type is erased at runtime, not from the .d.ts). * [024 — HellaNode marker properties are bare words (raw/static/componentScope/placeholder/dynamicComponent); __SLOT_N__ and __fragment__ parser tokens are KEPT __ on purpose — do not 'fix' them](entries/024.md) — Per guides/code.md (Naming->Variables, added 2026-07-17), internal marker PROPERTIES on HellaNode/HtmlPlaceholder/HtmlDynamicComponent dropped the __ prefix — __raw->raw, __static->static, __scope->componentScope, __placeholder->placeholder, __dynamicComponent->dynamicComponent (dom+ssr atomic, ssr reads `raw`). __SLOT_N__ and __fragment__ are STRING TOKENS injected into the HTML being parsed, not object properties — their __ is justified collision-resistance against arbitrary user text, so they are INTENTIONALLY KEPT. __scope->componentScope (not bare scope) because <th scope> is a real HTML attribute; componentScope mirrors ElementState.componentScope. · `triggers: underscore-marker, hella-node-fields, slot-token, fragment-token, componentscope, marker-rename` · `tags: arch, dom, ssr, naming, contract` · `type: decision`

* [026 — examples/ resolve @hellajs/* via ROOT node_modules walk-up (no declared deps); verify by RUNNING, never `bun add` into an example](entries/026.md) — Corrected 2026-07-28. * [027 — router({ url }) re-resolves on every call — the `!route().handler` init guard was skipping the path update for 2nd+ SSR requests (fixed)](entries/027.md) — Verified 2026-07-28 (fixed same day). router() init set the route path only when route().handler was unset (a client re-init protection), so a 2nd+ router({ url }) in one process kept the FIRST request's route — multi-request SSR rendered stale views. Fix: router.ts bypasses the guard when config.url is supplied (SSR explicit-url mode always re-resolves); client re-init (no url) is unchanged. Without it, per-request SSR (Bun.serve or a Vite SSR middleware calling router({ url }) per request) is broken after the first request. · `triggers: router-ssr, router-url-option, per-request-ssr, router-init-guard` · `tags: arch, ssr, router, isomorphic` · `type: correction`
* [028 — JSX component children arrive as an array (`children: [child]`); html\`\` as a single child — ssr's walkChild/walkChildGen must iterate arrays, not just single children (fixed)](entries/028.md) — Verified 2026-07-28 (fixed same day). babel-plugin-hellajs compiles <Comp>{child}</Comp> to component(Comp, { children: [child] }) — an ARRAY; html\`\` compiles <${Comp}>${child}</${Comp}> to props.children = child (single). The ssr walkers classified only single children and DROPPED arrays (fell through to 'nothing'), so JSX <Suspense>{...}</Suspense> streamed an EMPTY staged <template>. Fix: walkChild (sync, lib/ssr.ts) and walkChildGen (async, lib/internal/walk.ts) now branch on Array.isArray → delegate to walkChildren/walkChildrenGen; html\`\` single-child output is byte-identical (parity preserved). · `triggers: ssr-component-children, jsx-array-children, suspense-streaming, ssr-walker, html-vs-jsx` · `tags: arch, ssr, dom, jsx, babel, contract` · `type: correction`
* [029 — Vite SSR runs vite-plugin-hellajs on the server entry — ssrLoadModule('/src/server.tsx') transforms server-side JSX to HellaNode; a configureServer middleware streams the SSR HTML](entries/029.md) — Verified 2026-07-28. The vite-plugin-hellajs transform (enforce: 'pre', transforms .tsx/.ts/.jsx/.js, skips node_modules) runs in BOTH Vite's client pipeline AND its SSR pipeline, so server.ssrLoadModule('/src/server.tsx') yields a module whose JSX is already HellaNode (not React createElement). Runnable pattern: vite.config.js adds a plugin with configureServer(server) that, for each app route, ssrLoadModules the server entry (which exports render(url): ReadableStream<string>), writes chunks to the Node res, and hands module/asset URLs (/src/*, /@*, /node_modules/*, file extensions) to Vite via next(). This avoids Bun's built-in JSX (React runtime) silently taking over server JSX (wrong output, no error). · `triggers: vite-ssr, jsx-server-entry, ssrloadmodule, vite-plugin-server, configure-server-ssr` · `tags: arch, ssr, dom, jsx, vite, plugin` · `type: decision`
* [030 — <Suspense> resolves Promise-returning children on client fresh-mount (universal boundary) — one-shot, errors bubble, resource + reactive child for reactive](entries/030.md) — Verified 2026-07-28, re-verified 2026-08-21 (Show references removed — no such export; hydrate degradation added). <Suspense>'s fresh-mount branch (Suspense.ts, the non-hydrate path) resolves a thenable child: renders `fallback` → awaits → swaps resolved content in before the anchor (mirrors Lazy; the suspend block is the file-local suspendChild helper, shared since 2026-08-21 with the hydrate degradation path; cancellation via state.suspenseCleanup). On rejection the pending fallback is removed and the error bubbles to the nearest error:fallback/error:boundary/onError via dispatchError (React/Solid/Vue parity; unlike Lazy which keeps errors local). Sync children render directly. ONE-SHOT at mount — NOT reactive: the child function runs once and <Suspense> does NOT re-suspend when a signal it reads changes, because HellaJS's `resource` is not Suspense-aware (exposes isLoading()/error()/data() for an explicit reactive child branching on them) and a reactive raw-Promise Suspense would be a cache-less parallel path. For reactive async use resource + a reactive child (e.g. ${() => user.isLoading() ? fallback : user.data()}) — there is NO <Show> component. Fixes the [object Promise]/[object Object] fresh-mount bug (resolveNode had stringified the child). JSX wraps the child in `children: [fn]` (memory 028), so the branch UNWRAPS a length-1 array before evaluating — else the producer is stringified; TEST BOTH `html`` ` (single child) AND JSX (`children:[fn]`) shapes. Server path (ssrStream stages <template>) unchanged; the hydrate path gained a stageMissing degradation on 2026-08-21 — a seen sentinel whose staged <template> never arrived (interrupted stream) flags the ctx and <Suspense> re-suspends client-side with fresh-mount semantics. · `triggers: suspense-client-async, suspense-fresh-mount, suspense-reactive-resuspend, suspense-error-bubble` · `tags: arch, dom, suspense, streaming, contract` · `type: decision`
* [031 — dispatchError does NOT populate context.config — caller must; from a context with no pre-resolved boundary (isDynamic fn(parent)) use resolveErrorConfig(origin), NOT getBoundaryConfig(parent)](entries/031.md) — Verified 2026-07-28. dispatchError(error, context) finds the boundary itself via findBoundary(context.element) but passes context.config through AS-IS — it does not re-derive it — and handlers read context.config.fallback to render error UI (e.g. fallbackHandler in tests/helpers.ts: onError((e,ctx) => ctx.config?.fallback?.(e) ?? def)). ErrorContext.config is optional. render.ts's reactive-child effect passes config: getBoundaryConfig(currentBoundary) because currentBoundary (the pre-resolved nearest boundary) is in scope. But an isDynamic component's fn(parent) has NO currentBoundary — getBoundaryConfig(parent) peeks ONLY parent's own state.errorConfig (undefined when parent isn't itself a boundary, the common case), leaving context.config empty and SILENTLY breaking error:fallback. Use resolveErrorConfig(parent) instead — it walks parentElement up returning the first errorConfig of any kind (the semantically-intended helper), so the nearest boundary's error:fallback reaches the handler. · `triggers: dispatcherror-context-config, isdynamic-error-bubble, resolveerrorconfig, error-fallback-config` · `tags: arch, dom, errors, contract` · `type: decision`
* [032 — ssrStream flushes staged <Suspense> swaps concurrently in completion order — hydrate resolves staged templates by getElementById (id, not document position), so order-independent emission needs no reorder buffer](entries/032.md) — Verified 2026-07-30, re-verified 2026-09-01 (pull-driven). The pull that observes the main generator's completion kicks the staged <Suspense> collection: Promise.all drains every pending region concurrently, and each drain APPENDS its <template id="hsN"> to an internal flush queue the moment its own async work completes (completion order, not tree order), so a slow region no longer holds back a faster sibling — parked pulls wake on append and deliver one queue chunk per pull (every enqueue happens inside pull; backpressure). Safe because hydrate's swapSuspenseStage resolves each template via document.getElementById(sentinel.nodeValue) — id-keyed, position-independent — so emitting the staged templates in any order is hydrate-correct. A `done` flag shared by pull()/cancel() suppresses late flush work after cancel/error; a rejecting swap is caught per drain (warn + skip — fallback/sentinel remain; the stream still completes). Refines the streaming model (memory 033); does not supersede it. · `triggers: ssrstream-swap-collection, concurrent-suspense-streaming, completion-order-streaming, hydrate-template-id-lookup` · `tags: arch, ssr, streaming, suspense, hydration` · `type: decision`
* [033 — Progressive <Suspense> streaming via inline $hs swap scripts (React/Solid parity) — supersedes the β no-inline-script model](entries/033.md) — Verified 2026-07-30 (browser-confirmed). ssrStream emits a one-time $hs bootstrap, then each staged <template> is followed by <script>$hs("hsN")</script> that swaps the fallback for the resolved content the MOMENT it arrives — progressive content reveal (React $RC / Solid _$HY parity). hydrate still runs ONCE and adopts the already-swapped nodes; swapSuspenseStage is now the no-script/HappyDOM fallback (runs only when the inline script hasn't, e.g. in tests). $hs lives as the HS_SWAP_SCRIPT const in packages/ssr/lib/ssrStream.ts (emitted inline — memory 014 clears this vs the zero-runtime invariant; ssr can't import dom). Supersedes memory 015's β framing ('no inline script, swapSuspenseStage swaps at hydrate, α stays a future option'). What did NOT change: hydrate is still one pass; α-style per-segment SELECTIVE HYDRATION OF INTERACTIVITY (handlers going live per-segment) is still the gap — we do progressive CONTENT reveal, not progressive interactivity. · `triggers: progressive-suspense-streaming, inline-swap-script, hs-bootstrap, suspense-progressive-reveal, alpha-beta-superseded` · `tags: arch, ssr, streaming, suspense, hydration, dom` · `type: decision`
* [034 — HappyDOM hydrate/swap tests must assert full container.textContent (or scan stray text nodes) — querySelector('#x').textContent passes while [object Promise] sits right next to the matched node](entries/034.md) — Verified 2026-07-30 (a bug shipped to the browser under a green test). A hydrate/swap test that asserts only `container.querySelector('#root b').textContent === 'resolved'` passes GREEN even when a getter is re-evaluated into a Promise and stringified to a stray `[object Promise]` text node appended right beside the matched element. The Progressive-Suspense feature's first HappyDOM hydrate-integration test did exactly this and missed the `[object Promise]` regression the user caught in the browser. Fix: hydrate/swap tests must assert on full `container.textContent` (or explicitly assert `not.toContain('[object Promise]')` / scan for unexpected text nodes), not just a queried element's text. Generalizes: any test covering a code path that resolves a child value should check the WHOLE container for stringification artifacts, since a correctly-rendered node co-located with a stringified one is invisible to a targeted querySelector. · `triggers: happydom-hydrate-test, object-promise-stringification, hydrate-test-assertion, stray-text-node, swap-test-coverage` · `tags: testing, ssr, dom, hydration, suspense` · `type: correction`
* [035 — afterMount + descendant isMounted fire synchronously at the end of mount()/hydrate() via an internal flush(); the scoped MutationObserver only catches LATER dynamic additions, and registry.addHook immediate-fires afterMount on already-mounted nodes](entries/035.md) — afterMount/isMounted only run inside processMountQueue; the observer misses the initial attach, so mount()/hydrate() flush internally and the handle's flush() is an optional idempotent escape hatch. registry.addHook fires afterMount immediately when registered on an already-mounted node. · `triggers: aftermount-timing, mount-handle-flush, processmountqueue, hydrate-lifecycle` · `tags: arch, dom, lifecycle, contract` · `type: decision`
* [036 — A reactive getter resolving to an ARRAY of children (e.g. `items.map(t => <li>{t}</li>)`) must be walked element-by-element in ssr's resolved-value classification — distinct from the direct-child-array case (memory 028); else SSR stringifies it to [object Object] while the DOM renders it (parity gap, fixed)](entries/036.md) — Verified 2026-08-09 (fixed same day). Inside the `typeof child === 'function'` branch, walkChild (sync, lib/ssr.ts) and walkChildGen (async, lib/internal/walk.ts) classify the RESOLVED value. A getter like `() => items.map(t => <li>{t}</li>)` resolves to a HellaNode[] — `typeof === 'object'` but no `.tag` — so without an `Array.isArray(resolved)` branch it fell through to `${resolved}` → `[object Object],...`. Fix: both walkers now branch on `Array.isArray(resolved)` → walkChildren/walkChildrenGen, mirroring dom's resolveNode (which checks Array.isArray FIRST). Output is byte-identical to the ForEach case (`<!--[--><li>1</li>…<!--]-->`, one region pair wraps the array). This is a DIFFERENT code path from memory 028 (top-level `Array.isArray(child)` for direct component children `[child]`) — two classification paths, same symptom class; both must handle arrays. · `triggers: ssr-resolved-array-getter, object-object-ssr, walkchild-resolved-classification, map-idiom-ssr` · `tags: arch, ssr, dom, contract` · `type: correction`
* [037 — Attribute and child reactivity share ONE runtime discriminator — isFunction(value); the babel maybeReactive layer (applied to element children AND element attribute values, never components) is what makes a call-containing value reactive. Runtime html cannot wrap.](entries/037.md) — Verified 2026-08-09. dom's per-binding reactivity gates on a single check — isFunction(value) at render.ts mountNode (props loop) and reactive.ts bind. A function value registers an effect (reactive); a primitive/array/object renders once (static). The babel maybeReactive layer (src/utils/reactive.mjs) wraps call-containing expressions into thunks so they pass that gate. As of 2026-08-09, maybeReactive is applied to JSX element children (children.mjs), JSX element attribute values (attributes.mjs, props branch ONLY — prefixed keys on:/e:/hook:/error: excluded), and compiled html`` element children + attributes (ast.mjs) — every site gated !isComponent. Excluded everywhere: component children/props, prefixed keys, and any expression already a function at top level (double-wrap guard). Runtime html (lib/html.ts) interpolates raw values via cloneWithValues and cannot wrap — explicit () => required. Signal-ref loophole: {signal} is reactive because a signal IS a function; {signal()} is reactive only via babel wrapping (static under runtime html, no compiler). · `triggers: attribute-reactivity, isfunction-reactivity-gate, maybereactive-application, runtime-html-cannot-wrap, signal-ref-vs-called` · `tags: arch, dom, babel, contract` · `type: decision`
* [038 — Never write path globs (dir/*.ext) inside JSDoc block comments — the glob's */ terminates the comment early](entries/038.md) — A glob like `examples/*/tutorial.mdx` or `docs/**/*.mdx` inside a docstring embeds the comment terminator and breaks parsing; reword to prose (e.g. "the tutorial.mdx inside each examples/<name>/"). · `triggers: jsdoc-glob, block-comment-terminator, guard-script-docstring, scripts-docstring-edit` · `tags: toolchain, scripts, docs` · `type: correction`
* [039 — Test core graph retention with WeakRef canaries flowing through the computed's return value — dead-expression canaries optimize out](entries/039.md) — Reactive-node state (rd/rs/cbc) is closure-private, so the only way to observe internal retention via public API is to capture a canary object in the computed's closure AND reference it in the value the computed returns (so it lands in cbc), keep the source signals alive, drop all refs to the computed and its subscriber, run Bun.gc(true) at least twice, then check weakRef.deref(); a bare `held;` expression statement in the closure optimizes away and yields a false "no leak". · `triggers: core-leak-test, weakref-canary, computed-auto-gc, retention-probe` · `tags: core, testing, memory-leak, reactive-graph` · `type: decision`
* [040 — Comparison-doc competitor research falls back to npm registry tarballs when web fetch fails](entries/040.md) — When Bundlephobia/WebFetch is unavailable or returns empty, ground every competitor claim by downloading `registry.npmjs.org` tarballs and reading the published source directly — more authoritative than docs pages anyway. · `triggers: competitor-research, comparison-doc, bundlephobia-failed, web-fetch-failed` · `tags: tooling, research, comparison` · `type: decision`
* [041 — A hand-rolled isDynamic test component used as `<${Dyn}>` in an html`` template must be a PROPS-CALLABLE FACTORY — the template invokes Dyn(mergedProps) at build time, so a bare `(parent) => …` fn fails with "parent.appendChild is not a function"](entries/041.md) — Verified 2026-08-21 (cost a red test in dom coverage work). html``'s cloneWithValues invokes a dynamic component as Comp(mergedProps) at template-build time (passthrough when isDynamic) — the fn it RETURNS is what appendToParent later calls with the real parent. So a test component authored as a bare `((parent) => {…}) as (() => void) & { isDynamic: boolean }` receives the PROPS OBJECT, not a parent: its appendChild call throws TypeError: parent.appendChild is not a function, stack through cloneWithValues. Correct shape: `const Dyn = () => { const fn = (parent: Element) => {…} as (() => void) & { isDynamic: boolean }; fn.isDynamic = true; return fn; };` — the factory takes props (ignore them), returns the isDynamic fn. The bare-fn shape only works when handed to a reactive child (`${() => toggle()}` resolving to the fn), never via `<${Dyn}>`. · `triggers: isdynamic-test-component, html-dynamic-component-factory, appendchild-is-not-a-function, cloneWithValues-props-call` · `tags: testing, dom, html-template, isdynamic` · `type: decision`
* [042 — A test asserting the CATCH side of a `.then(fn).catch(fn)` chain on an ALREADY-REJECTED promise must wait past TWO microtask hops — a single `await delay()` resumes the test before the catch runs and false-fails](entries/042.md) — Verified 2026-08-21 empirically (dom unit 08, degradation-rejection test). `Promise.reject(x).then(f).catch(g)` settles g only after two microtask ticks (the .then callback rejects first, then .catch fires); `await delay()` is ONE microtask hop (utils/test-helpers.js: `delay() => Promise.resolve()`), so the test resumes between the hops — handler call-count reads 0, fallback still mounted. A resolved (non-rejected) chain settles in one hop, which is why the happy-path twin passes with the same wait. Fix per guides/tests.md: a real-time wait `await delay(50)` (or any macrotask boundary) — never a double `await delay(); await delay()` (banned). Recognizer: an error-path assertion that reads exactly one microtask 'too early' while its resolve-path twin is green. · `triggers: catch-assertion-too-early, sync-rejected-promise-chain, microtask-hop-count, delay-insufficient` · `tags: testing, async, microtask, bun-test` · `type: decision`
* [043 — A braced switch-case with its own const in dom's coverage-instrumented bundle leaves the case's CLOSING BRACE counted as uncovered — restructure to an unbraced case with a hoisted let before chasing "missing coverage"](entries/043.md) — Verified 2026-08-21 (dom unit 08). Adding `case "suspense": { const swapped = swapSuspenseStage(...); … }` (braced block, own binding) to `hydrateDynamic` produced exactly ONE uncovered line in `bun coverage dom` — the bundle line holding the case's closing brace `}`, with every real statement covered. istanbul counts the brace-only line as an uncovered statement location when the case introduces a block scope. Fix: hoist the binding above the switch (`let swappedStage: { nodes: Node[]; missing: boolean };`) and use an unbraced case — the sibling cases in the same switch are all unbraced, so this also matches house style. Check the uncovered bundle line's content with sed before writing a test for it — if it is a lone `}`, no test can cover it. · `triggers: uncovered-closing-brace, braced-switch-case-coverage, istanbul-case-block, phantom-uncovered-line` · `tags: testing, coverage, istanbul, dom` · `type: decision`
* [044 — Wrapping a ReadableStream requires an up-front getReader() — for-await locks the source stream and breaks cancel propagation](entries/044.md) — A ReadableStream wrapper that pipes a source stream (like docStream over ssrStream) must acquire `const reader = body.getReader()` before start() and drain via a manual read-loop; `for await` over the source takes its async iterator (locking the stream), so a later `body.cancel(reason)` in the wrapper's cancel() throws `TypeError: Invalid state: ReadableStream is locked` (ERR_INVALID_STATE) — cancel through the held reader instead (`reader.cancel(reason)`), which still reaches the source's cancel callback. · `triggers: readablestream-wrapper, stream-cancel-propagation, for-await-stream-lock, docstream-cancel` · `tags: arch, ssr, streaming, contract` · `type: decision`
* [045 — ssr public API consolidated for the v2 major — `ssr` callable namespace (`ssr.async`/`ssr.stream`) + type-overloaded `doc`; ssrAsync/ssrStream/docStream names deleted, no aliases](entries/045.md) — The major collapses @hellajs/ssr from 5 exports to 2. `ssr` is a callable namespace — non-exported `SsrFn` interface in lib/ssr.ts + `Object.assign(ssrImpl, { async: ssrAsync, stream: ssrStream })`; the member impls stay in lib/ssrAsync.ts / lib/ssrStream.ts, exported `@internal` (attach-not-move — keeps per-file coverage mapping and the walkChild/walkChildGen parity comments co-located). `doc` is one overload pair discriminated by `body` type (`string` → string; `ReadableStream<string>` → ReadableStream) with `mount` legal in both modes; DocStreamOptions deleted, DocOptions.body widened. No transitional aliases — the major IS the deletion moment. Rejected alternatives: boolean flags (`ssr(n,{async:true})` breaks dynamic mode selection — non-literal booleans match no overload, and `useStream ? ssr.stream : ssr.async` is the composable form); `doc.stream` namespace (ceremony over something the type system already discriminates); aliases during the window. · `triggers: ssr-namespace, ssr-async-member, ssr-stream-member, doc-overload, api-consolidation, ssrasync-deleted, ssrstream-deleted, docstream-deleted` · `tags: arch, ssr, api, breaking-change, streaming` · `type: decision`
* [046 — A missing-body test against an overloaded function must cast to a concrete overload shape — `{} as DocOptions` (union body) matches no overload once overloads exist](entries/046.md) — When a function gains overloads (e.g. doc's body-type pair), a negative test like `doc({} as DocOptions)` fails tsc with TS2769 ("No overload matches this call") because `{}` doesn't satisfy EITHER overload's narrowed `body` intersection — cast to a specific overload shape instead (`{} as DocOptions & { body: string }`), which type-checks and still exercises the runtime body-required throw. · `triggers: overload-negative-test, ts2769-overload-cast, missing-body-test, union-options-cast` · `tags: testing, typescript, overloads, ssr` · `type: decision`
* [047 — HappyDOM stopImmediatePropagation() does NOT set cancelBubble — delegated-walk stop tests must set both flags](entries/047.md) — HappyDOM deviates from the DOM spec — cancelBubble stays false after stopImmediatePropagation() (true after stopPropagation()), so tests of the delegated on: walk's cancelBubble check must call both stop methods as a real browser would. · `triggers: happydom-stopimmediate, cancelbubble, delegated-walk-stop, stoppropagation-test` · `tags: testing, dom, events, happydom` · `type: correction`
* [048 — Run root `bun bundle` before building/measuring any example after a ref switch — examples bundle against gitignored packages/*/dist, which survives checkout](entries/048.md) — Examples that bundle @hellajs/* (e.g. examples/bench rollup) resolve each package via its package.json main → packages/*/dist, which is gitignored and SURVIVES git checkout — switching refs without a prior root `bun bundle` silently builds/measures the PREVIOUS ref's dist. · `triggers: examples-dist, bench-ab, ref-switch-build, stale-dist` · `tags: arch, examples, build, workspaces` · `type: decision`
* [049 — Green happy-dom CSS asserts do not prove browser-valid CSS — invalid structures parse to silent empty rules in BOTH engines, and happy-dom diverges from Chrome on at-rule support and cssText serialization](entries/049.md) — Verified 2026-07-30 via Playwright + happy-dom A/B. Structurally invalid CSS (`@font-face{{…}}`, `@media …{{…}}` — double-brace output from an empty-selector emitter) is silently accepted as an EMPTY rule by happy-dom AND real Chrome: declarations drop, no error, substring asserts stay green (this shipped for the life of @hellajs/css). happy-dom also diverges from Chrome: insertRule REJECTS valid `@layer`/`@starting-style` (Chrome accepts), and cssText re-serializes (`0`→`0px`, `from`→`0%`, quoted font-family loses quotes, trailing `;}` before `}`, `rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.8)` spaces). So: assert generated output in exact form (guides/tests.md anti-pattern), verify at-rule composition via the server text return or a real browser, and never treat a happy-dom-green CSSOM test as proof of browser validity. · `triggers: happydom-css-text, invalid-css-masked, at-rule-assert, cssom-serialization` · `tags: testing, css, happydom, cssom` · `type: decision`
* [050 — Probe cross-package reactivity from dist bundles only — mixing source and dist imports splits the reactive graph silently](entries/050.md) — Importing a reactive primitive from core SOURCE (e.g. `./packages/core/lib/index.ts`) while the package under probe resolves `@hellajs/core` to its DIST bundle creates two disjoint reactive graphs — effects never observe writes and effect-count verification reads false negatives with no error; always probe with both sides on dist (`@hellajs/store/bundle` + `@hellajs/core`), exactly as tests do. · `triggers: runtime-probing-store, dist-vs-source-imports, effect-count-verification, cross-package-probes` · `tags: arch, testing, core, bundling` · `type: decision`
* [051 — Store provenance — signals and user functions are shape-indistinguishable; the non-enumerable settableRegistry on every store is the single discriminator](entries/051.md) — In @hellajs/store, a core signal and a preserved user function are both plain functions with no marker — any feature that must know whether a property key is signal-backed (update() writes, snapshot function-preservation, future paths) MUST consult the store's settable-keys registry (non-enumerable symbol `settableRegistry` on every store object, threaded through composition), never `isFunction(initial[key])`, which silently skips every composed leaf because a composed store's `initial` has function-valued data properties. · `triggers: store-provenance, settable-keys-registry, composed-store-updates, snapshot-discriminator` · `tags: arch, store, composition` · `type: decision`
* [052 — cleanAbort aborts the predecessor controller on every transition — a settled request's stale timeout timer can never kill a later request](entries/052.md) — In packages/resource, every currentAbortController assignment routes through cleanAbort(), which aborts the predecessor and thereby clears its timeout timer — so per-request timers/listeners cannot cross-request misfire; verify transitions before asserting abort-wiring Breaks. · `triggers: cleanAbort, abort-wiring, wireRequestControls, stale-timer` · `tags: resource, arch` · `type: correction`
* [053 — Moving a code block between package docs breaks doc-snippets on BOTH ends — make moved blocks self-sufficient and re-check the source doc's remaining import coverage](entries/053.md) — doc-snippets models each doc as one module (imports hoisted + merged per-doc, blocks nested-scoped so later blocks read earlier declarations with concrete types) — a block move can strand name references in the source doc and type-collide in the target doc. · `triggers: doc-section-move, snippet-relocation, doc-snippets-failure, doc-split, ts2552-after-move` · `tags: docs, toolchain, doc-snippets` · `type: decision`
* [054 — Reference nav order mirrors each package's docs/index.mdx API list — usefulness order, low-level tier last](entries/054.md) — docs/src/nav.ts reference entries must list symbols in exactly the order of the matching packages/*/docs/index.mdx "### API" list — usefulness (primary API first, reset*/cleanup utils last), not A–Z; low-level APIs ($ref, $collection, component, registry) sink to the bottom of dom. · `triggers: reference-nav, nav-order, new-reference-page, package-index-mdx` · `tags: docs, nav` · `type: decision`
* [055 — Docs-site daisyUI/Tailwind classes used only in imported package-docs/examples MDX need explicit @source lines in docs/src/global.css — globs are stylesheet-relative and must end in a recursive file tail](entries/055.md) — Tailwind v4 auto-detection stops at the docs/ Vite root, so any class used only in packages/*/docs or examples/*/tutorial.mdx is tree-shaken from the build; the @source globs that fix it resolve against docs/src/ (the stylesheet's dir) and a wildcard glob with a directory tail matches zero files unless it ends in /**/*. · `triggers: docs-css-missing, tailwind-source, daisyui-class-dropped, imported-mdx-styles` · `tags: docs, build, css, tailwind` · `type: decision`
* [056 — Run empirical package checks as `bun -e` from packages/<pkg> — @hellajs/* subpath imports do not resolve from /tmp scratch files](entries/056.md) — Quick behavioral probes of a workspace package (constructor names, render output, public-API sanity) run as `cd packages/<pkg> && bun -e '…'` with dynamic imports — a scratch .ts outside the repo tree fails to resolve `@hellajs/<pkg>/bundle` because workspace linking only works via node_modules walk-up from inside the repo. · `triggers: empirical-probe, scratch-script, subpath-import, bun-e` · `tags: toolchain, workspaces, testing` · `type: decision`
* [058 — deleteRule rebasing landed — indexMap stored indexes stay exact after every removal; per-id hosted sheets are an architectural choice, not a staleness containment](entries/058.md) — Every successful deleteRule calls rebaseIndexes(qid, i) in packages/css/lib/internal/sheet.ts (decrements same-sheet `${qid}:`-prefixed indexMap entries above i), so multi-rule removeCss and interleaved removals are exact; sharing a sheet's index space across APIs is viable again, though hosted sheets remain one <style> per sheet id. · `triggers: removeRule-rebase, removeCss-rule-leak, sheet-indexmap, hosted-sheets-per-id` · `tags: arch, css` · `type: correction`
* [059 — In a dirty worktree the pre-change baseline is the session-read file, not git-checkout HEAD — reconstruct, rebuild, measure, restore](entries/059.md) — To attribute a coverage/test delta to your change, back up the edited file, write back the exact pre-edit content from your session read, explicitly bun-bundle, run the scoped test command coverage runs internally, then restore the backup and rebuild — never `git checkout --` a file when the worktree carries uncommitted user changes. · `triggers: coverage-baseline, pre-change-baseline, dirty-worktree` · `tags: workflow, testing` · `type: decision`
* [060 — hydrateNode tag comparison is exact-case for foreign-namespace elements — SVG/MathML parsers keep authored tag case, so uppercase-folding false-mismatches every camelCase tag](entries/060.md) — DOM parsers (browsers and HappyDOM alike) preserve authored case for elements created in a foreign namespace — innerHTML `<svg><clipPath>` yields tagName "clipPath" (SVGClipPathElement, SVG ns) — so any hydrate/adopt tag comparison must be exact-case when the existing element's namespaceURI is non-HTML (`tagMatches` in packages/dom/lib/internal/hydrate.ts); folding to `tag.toUpperCase()` compares "clipPath" against "CLIPPATH", warns a false mismatch, and replaceMismatch subtree-replaces a perfectly matching server node. Companion facts from the same fix — element creation must go through `createElementNS` under foreign-ns parents or tags mount as HTMLUnknownElement and render nothing (`childNamespaceOf`/`HTML_NS` in packages/dom/lib/internal/render.ts); HappyDOM has no MathMLElement class, so MathML tests assert `namespaceURI`, not constructors; and lib.dom types `localName`/`namespaceURI` on `Element` only — a helper typed `(parent: Node | null)` must cast to `Element` before reading them or tsc fails TS2339. · `triggers: hydrate-tag-compare, svg-namespace, tagmatches, foreign-namespace` · `tags: dom, hydrate, svg` · `type: decision`
* [061 — A new worktree cut mid-unit can inherit a red HEAD — carry the uncommitted shared helper verbatim, run the baseline, flag the carry for drop](entries/061.md) — When a worktree's baseline fails on a foreign package because a committed test imports a helper that exists only in the main tree's uncommitted changes, copy the user's current shared-helper file into the worktree uncommitted (never edit it), verify attribution first, and record that the carried file must be dropped when its owning unit lands. · `triggers: worktree-baseline, foreign-baseline, carried-helper` · `tags: process, git, testing` · `type: decision`
* [062 — Torn git index after a failed hook commit — phantom hash + mass staged deletions, files intact on disk: rm the index file and reset; plain `git reset` fails](entries/062.md) — A nested `git commit` inside the post-commit hook can die with `Error building trees` / `invalid object <hash>` and leave the worktree index torn (tiny file, hundreds of staged deletions, a hash no tree references) — diagnose index-vs-store via `git ls-tree <commit> <path>` against the phantom, then recover with `rm "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/index" && git reset -q`; do NOT conclude object-store corruption and do NOT start with `git reset`, which fails on the phantom. · `triggers: torn-index, error-building-trees, phantom-hash` · `tags: process, git, tooling` · `type: correction`
* [063 — dist/bundle.js inlines lib — @hellajs/{pkg}/{file} subpath imports are separate module instances from /bundle imports](entries/063.md) — Every package's dist/bundle.js contains its own compiled copy of each lib module, so a test that imports values from @hellajs/{pkg}/bundle and internals from a @hellajs/{pkg}/{file} subpath reads two different module instances — keep all test imports of the package under test on /bundle; internal module state is unobservable from tests by design. · `triggers: subpath-import, module-instance, bundle-import, test-import-source` · `tags: arch, testing, toolchain` · `type: decision`
* [064 — Deterministic GC/WeakRef assertions in bun — drop refs, await delay(0) macrotask turn, then Bun.gc(true)x3; GC outside the activation that used the object (JSC retains its closure graph while suspended)](entries/064.md) — In bun/JSC, a WeakRef target stays reachable from scheduled-but-unprocessed async machinery, so Bun.gc alone flakes — null/drop every reference, await delay(0) for a macrotask turn, then Bun.gc(true) at least twice (three used here). Separately, a suspended async activation conservatively retains the closure graph of any object whose methods it called — even after every reference is nulled — so a WeakRef deref run inside that still-live function false-pins; the retention dissolves the moment the accessing function returns (no hellajs-owned reference exists — verified), and it is not reproducible with a no-core closure graph, so GC tests must do create/access in one function and deref after it returns, never in the same live test body. · `triggers: weakref-gc-test, bun-gc-flake, macrotask-flush, resource-graph-pin` · `tags: testing, resource, memory-leak` · `type: decision`
* [065 — resetResource clears onlineCallbacks but never resets onlineStatus — online/offline leaks across tests](entries/065.md) — resource's onlineStatus is module state that survives resetTestState()/resetResource(); tests touching online behavior must dispatch their own state per test and restore online in afterEach. · `triggers: resource-online-test, onlinestatus, resetteststate, pausewhenoffline` · `tags: testing, resource` · `type: decision`
* [066 — route().path carries the query string (pathname + search) — tests and docs must expect the ?suffix, not the bare pathname](entries/066.md) — Verified 2026-08-14. The router's RouteInfo.path is the full path WITH search: router() seeds it from pathname + search (url option parsed or window.location), and resolve.ts commitMatch writes currentPath (which includes ?query) into the route signal. So resolving /users/7?q=1 yields route().path === '/users/7?q=1', not '/users/7'. active() strips the query itself (route.ts activeFn split('?')), and crumbs paths exclude it (resolve.ts builds crumb.path from pathWithoutQuery), but route().path itself keeps it. Any test or doc example asserting route().path after a query-carrying URL must include the ?suffix — the base-path unit's url-mode test failed one cycle on exactly this (expected '/users/7', received '/users/7?q=1'). · `triggers: route-path-query, routeinfo-path-shape, router-test-assertion, base-path` · `tags: arch, router, testing` · `type: decision`
* [067 — Bound template-literal token extraction per segment — `infer` slots cross `/` boundaries](entries/067.md) — In pattern-grammar types like ExtractParams, a cascade form (`${string}:${infer Param}?`) lets Param swallow `/` chars and produce bogus keys; token extraction must recurse per `/`-separated segment so every `infer` slot is bounded by one segment. · `triggers: extractparams, pattern-token-typing, template-literal-infer, optional-param-types` · `tags: types, router, pattern-grammar` · `type: decision`
* [068 — HappyDOM history APIs never move window.location.pathname off "blank" — popstate/back-forward simulations must first set window.location.href to a real URL](entries/068.md) — In the test env, pushState AND replaceState are no-ops for pathname until `window.location.href = "http://localhost/"` is assigned (guards.test.ts / scroll.test.ts beforeEach pattern); without it popstate handlers resolve the literal path "blank". · `triggers: popstate-test, hashchange-test, happydom-pathname, history-simulation` · `tags: testing, router, happydom, env` · `type: decision`
* [069 — Bun's coverage table renders an EMPTY uncovered-lines cell while %Lines < 100 — get the real line via the lcov reporter, and distrust a stale root coverage/lcov.info](entries/069.md) — When bun's scoped coverage table shows <100% lines but no uncovered line numbers, re-run with `--coverage-reporter=lcov --coverage-dir=<tmp>` and grep the router/package section's DA entries with hits 0; the repo-root `coverage/lcov.info` may be a stale cross-package artifact (dom/resource sections from an old unscoped run) — never attribute its contents to the current scoped run. · `triggers: bun-coverage-empty-cell, uncovered-line-not-listed, stale-lcov, coverage-reporter-lcov` · `tags: testing, coverage, bun, tooling` · `type: decision`
* [070 — delay() is one microtask hop (Promise.resolve) — insufficient for multi-hop promise chains; delay(0) (setTimeout 0) is the macrotask flush](entries/070.md) — delay() (no args) resolves via Promise.resolve(), a single microtask hop — enough for one microtask-bound continuation, NOT for draining chains (e.g. .then().catch(), async-generator yields, Bun.gc setup that needs queued callbacks settled). Use delay(0) (setTimeout 0 — macrotask boundary) or delay(N) for multi-hop draining. The tests guide's 'flush the microtask queue' is imprecise — it's one hop, not the queue. · `triggers: delay-insufficient, microtask-drain, async-test-timing, macrotask-flush, delay-zero` · `tags: testing, async, timing` · `type: decision`
* [071 — html`` templates type as `HellaNode | (() => HellaNode)` — ssr/ssr.async/ssr.stream calls need the `as HellaNode` cast while hydrate() accepts the union uncast](entries/071.md) — A tagged template passed straight to an ssr member fails tsc (TS2345) because html's declared return type is a union — append `as HellaNode` (the repo-wide test convention); hydrate(node, target) widens its param and takes the same expression uncast. · `triggers: ssr-test-cast, html-return-union, as-hellanode, ts2345-ssr` · `tags: testing, ssr, dom, types` · `type: decision`
* [072 — resource() never auto-fetches at creation — initialData seeds state, it does not suppress a fetch](entries/072.md) — Resources fetch only via explicit .fetch()/invalidate() or the refetchOnKeyChange effect (which fires at creation when set); initialData only populates data() with isLoading() false and status() 'idle' — so phrase SSR data-seeding as "the server's fetch is the fetch", never as "initialData kills/prevents the refetch". · `triggers: resource-initialdata, ssr-data-seeding, no-auto-fetch, doc-data-payload` · `tags: arch, resource, ssr, contract` · `type: decision`
